newsitem.title: UK: Analyst sees world sugar prices pressured near-term.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees world sugar prices pressured near-term.

text.p: World sugar prices should remain pressured in the near term as key producers clear old stocks amid sluggish demand from major players, a leading sugar economist said on Monday.

Exports were running significantly behind last year in Thailand and Brazil, two exporters with record crops, said Tony Hannah, chief economist at the London-based International Sugar Organization (ISO).

"In the near term prices should remain under pressure," Hannah said in a speech prepared for delivery at the Sixth World Sugar Farmers' Conference in Copenhagen, organised by the World Association of Beet and Cane Growers.
He added that average nominal prices for raw sugar were likely to stay within the range of 9 and 14 cents/lb which had been established since 1987.
Both Brazil and Thailand would want to clear stocks before sugar started to flow in quantity from new crops, July for Brazil and December for Thailand.
World markets would see more supply from other major exporters, such as Australia and South Africa, which were expecting record or near record crops this season.
Russia and China, key players on the demand side, were relatively absent, Hannah said.
"China has a much improved crop and demand is sluggish. Russia has good stocks, although it may begin to seek alternative sources of raw sugar unless shipments speed up from Cuba," he said.
But he noted that sugar was commodity that competed on price with High Fructose Corn Syrup (HFCS).

Prices sustained above 15 cents/lb for two or three years could cause the kind of investment in HFCS that occurred between 1975 and 1985, resulting in a permanent loss of market share for sugar, Hannah said.
